source_subtopic_title: Population, sample, target population and support
evidence_note: Population versus sample and support are taught; require a worked distinction between target population and observed support.

source_subtopic_title: Simple random, stratified, systematic and clustered sampling
evidence_note: Sampling designs and representativeness are discussed; verify design-specific estimator and standard-error practice.
Sampling distribution and standard error are introduced; the complete sampling-distribution concept needs a checked worked example.
Interval arithmetic is covered; mean, median, proportion and slope as distinct targets need explicit comparison.
Coverage interpretation and common misinterpretation are included; confirm learner practice explains the repeated-sampling meaning.

source_subtopic_title: Standard error, dependence and effective sample size
evidence_note: Dependence caveat is explicit; effective sample size is not yet established as a worked calculation.

source_subtopic_title: Bootstrap and block bootstrap with reproducible seed
evidence_note: Seeded bootstrap and block-bootstrap resampling logic are added; interval construction, block-length sensitivity and dependence validation remain incomplete.

source_subtopic_title: Null and alternative hypotheses; p-value interpretation
evidence_note: Conditional p-value interpretation and null/alternative framing are taught; verify with a learner response task.

source_subtopic_title: Type I and Type II errors; practical significance
evidence_note: Error types and practical significance are described; power is treated separately in lesson 5.4.5.
Benjamini–Hochberg is included; validate numerical example and explain dependence limitations.

source_subtopic_title: Pearson and Spearman correlation; non-causal interpretation
evidence_note: Pearson/Spearman and association-not-causation are explicit; check assumptions and comparison exercise.

source_subtopic_title: Simple OLS regression, slope units and assumptions
evidence_note: OLS and slope units are covered; assumptions need explicit diagnostic-to-assumption links.
Residual diagnostics are part of the workflow; verify an actual runnable residual-plot example.
Effect magnitude and practical relevance are discussed; add a numerical effect-size comparison if absent.
Qualitative power factors are described; no quantitative power calculation is claimed.
Mann–Whitney, signed-rank and Kruskal–Wallis choices/assumptions are explained; no computed rank-test result or effect-size interval.
